slides.title: Dispatch Copilot: launch decision, packaging and price

paragraphs.text: Dispatch Copilot: launch decision, packaging and price
Discussion document for the CEO and executive team, January 2027 planning
Brightwork
CEO and executive team
Synthetic benchmark data; all figures from the briefing pack
Executive summary
Launch Copilot in 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance, and in Q2 if Q4 win rates confirm the Routewise threat
Copilot helps dispatchers, but paid demand is far below the survey: a $149 add-on would add about $2.5M of ARR, not $8M
–	Beta accounts scheduled 11% more jobs per dispatcher-hour, but they were volunteers
–	14% of beta accounts bought at $149, compared with 46% of survey respondents who said they would
–	At the paywall rate, the add-on brings under a third of the $8M forecast
A Pro plan at $12 more per seat, with 600 requests per seat included, reaches more accounts and keeps margin above 75%
–	A flat $149 fee draws heavy users: the top tenth would cost $131 a month to serve
–	At the 2023 tier's 33% take-up, Pro adds about $2.9M of ARR, against $2.5M for the add-on
–	The NRR target needs 26% take-up; uncapped, margin breaks at 5,300 requests per account
Timing turns on Routewise: launch in Q2 if Q4 win rates stay near 37%, and rewrite mobile first if they recover
–	Routewise's AI puts at most about $0.6M of new ARR a year at risk
–	Mobile reliability drives 27% of churn, 4.5 times as much as AI
–	Delaying Copilot costs more only if Routewise's AI, not its discount, is taking deals

slides.title: At the paywall rate, the add-on would bring about $2.5M of new ARR, under a third of the CPO's forecast

paragraphs.text: 1 Demand    2 Package    3 Timing
At the paywall rate, the add-on would bring about $2.5M of new ARR, under a third of the CPO's forecast
New ARR from a $149 add-on, $ millions, first year after launch
customer accounts today

add-on price per account per year ($149 × 12)

Even $2.5M is an upper estimate, for three reasons
▪	The 14% comes from volunteers that are larger and more active than the base; take-up across all accounts is likely lower
▪	The forecast's 46% is stated intent from a 6% response rate, skewed to larger accounts
▪	No discounts, and buyers stay for the full year
▪	Gross revenue before inference cost; buyers are heavy users (next section)
1  The CPO forecast recomputed: 9,800 accounts × 46% × $149 × 12 = $8.06M, the 'about $8M' in the proposal
Sources: Brightwork briefing pack (synthetic); team analysis

slides.title: If a third of accounts move up, as in 2023, a per-seat Pro plan adds about $2.9M of ARR

paragraphs.text: 1 Demand    2 Package    3 Timing
If a third of accounts move up, as in 2023, a per-seat Pro plan adds about $2.9M of ARR
New ARR from a Pro plan at $12 more per seat per month, $ millions, run-rate after one year
customer accounts today
moved to the 2023 higher tier within a year (company history)
Pro premium per account per year: 6.2 seats × $12 × 12
new ARR, equal to 5.0 percentage points of NRR on $57.6M
The estimate rests on three assumptions
▪	A third of accounts move to Pro within a year, as 33% did after the 2023 higher-tier launch; Pro includes Copilot, the earlier tier did not
▪	Accounts that move have the base average of 6.2 seats and pay $12 more per seat per month
▪	No change in Core churn or seat counts from the launch; all new ARR comes from existing accounts, so it counts towards NRR
An average account pays $74.4 a month for Pro, half the $149 add-on, and Pro costs less for any account under 12.4 seats
1  The 2023 tier did not include AI; whether Copilot pulls more or fewer accounts up is the main uncertainty (next page)
Sources: Brightwork briefing pack (synthetic); team analysis
